messages:
Alex: Quick sync for Nimbus POC (FinOps). Need to lock hosting approach + success criteria so we can finalize SOW. They require EU residency and want KMS + access logs. Also pushing on cost.
Maria: I can scope evals. Key asks: vector search recall targets, generation stability for billing explanations, and latency under typical query sizes (embedding requests small, gen up to 256 tokens).
Ben: Security checklist items we need answered from their side: data classification, required retention for audit logs (they asked 90 days), and who will manage KMS (BYOK vs Redwood-managed). I'll send our questionnaire and flag the KMS/BYOK options.
Sam: Hosting tradeoffs summary: Hosted: fastest to start (hours) but no contractual EU residency guarantee without addendum; Dedicated: predictable p95 latency, supports BYOK and SIEM integration out-of-the-box, trial turnaround ~3 business days after PO; Private: full control and on-prem but 4-6 weeks and sizeable set-up fee.
Jess: From product side, add routing/fallback plan to success criteria: if Dedicated capacity reaches 80% we fall back to hosted model variant with throttling policy. Need that in SOW.
Lina: Sales note on pricing: We can offer $3k hosted credits for 2-week POC. For Dedicated trial, propose a discounted committed week rate: €900/week (estimated) for a small cluster — need finance approval. Private not feasible for POC.
Maria: Proposed POC success criteria (customer-facing):
- Accuracy: vector recall@5 >= 0.9 on their gold queries
- Stability: <= 10% variance in answer top-1 for billing explanation prompts across 100 runs
- Latency: embeddings p95 < 120ms; gen p95 < 300ms at 256 tokens
- Reliability: <1% error rate during load tests
- Ops: KMS key rotation tested + logs to their SIEM (Splunk)
- Business: cost <= $3k credits or Dedicated discounted rate accepted
Ben: I'll request SOC2 Type II report, pen-test summary, and evidence of customer-managed key support. Also ask legal for data-residency addendum template (exhibit for EU-only processing).
Alex: Timeline proposal: 10 business days. Day0-2: contract + PO; Day3-5: infra + smoke; Day6-9: run load & evals; Day10: results & handoff. Is that realistic?
Sam: If we go Hosted it's realistic. Dedicated adds ~2 days for provisioning after PO. Private not in timeline.
Lina: I flagged a finance approval step: Dedicated trial discount needs manager sign-off. Will update by EOD.
Maria: Sharing the test curl and a small k6-like snippet we'll use for throughput testing: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rwd-gen-3","input":"Explain this charge in plain English","max_tokens":256}'```
And a pseudo-k6 loop: ```for (i=0;i<500;i++){ POST /v1/embeddings body: {model:'rwd-embed-2', input:['q'+i]} }```
Jess: Add acceptance criteria for UX: search 95th percentile for top-5 neighbors < 200ms when served from Dedicated in eu-west-1.
Ben: Client infosec contact is carol@nim-finops.com. I've CC'd them on the questionnaire. Waiting on SOC2 and pen-test.
Alex: Who owns the SOW language for fallback + data residency clause? I can draft but need legal review.
Lina: I'll prep the pricing line items for the SOW (hosted credits vs dedicated weekly rate).
infra-bot: Ticket created #POC-4622: Dedicated trial request (eu-west-1). Owner: Sam. Estimated provisioning window: 48-72h after PO.
Sam: I'll open a PR for the infra (ansible + cluster config) and tag @infra for expedited provisioning.
Maria: I'll upload the eval set and golden prompts by EOD. Also will include a small synthetic workload generator and measurement harness.
Jess: I'll draft the POC acceptance checklist that the customer signs: metrics, security ops handoffs, and fallback plan.
Alex: OK all — action owners: Maria (evals), Ben (infosec + docs), Sam (infra), Lina (pricing & finance), Jess (acceptance checklist), Alex (SOW + customer coordination). Will update Nimbus CRM with dates; ask Carol for PO by Thursday.
